title: Author Argo WorkflowTemplate pose-detection-build in declarative-config (ronaldraygun/gait-detection image)
description:
Create k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/pose-detection-build-workflowtemplate.yml in jedarden/declarative-config (clone at ~/declarative-config; git pull --rebase before touching, push immediately after commit).

Model on palm-reading-build-workflowtemplate.yml. IMPORTANT naming quirk: the repo is jedarden/pose-detection but the production image/deployment is gait-detection (live site gait.jedarden.com runs ronaldraygun/gait-detection:0.1.3 in namespace gait on apexalgo-iad). Keep template name pose-detection-build (matches repo), image name gait-detection (matches deployment).

Steps: test -> resolve-version -> docker-build (kaniko) -> update-declarative-config.
- test step (replaces the old GH Actions ci.yml test job): node:20-alpine (pin a specific tag/digest, not :latest), clone repo, npm ci && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build. activeDeadlineSeconds ~900, resources ~2Gi/1cpu. The old GH matrix tested node 18+20; a single node 20 run is sufficient
- Params: git-repo=jedarden/pose-detection, branch=main
- resolve-version: VERSION file does NOT exist in repo; initialize at 0.1.4 (deployed image is 0.1.3) and commit per palm-reading else-branch pattern. Git identity user.email github@jedarden.com / user.name jedarden; GH_TOKEN from secret github-webhook-secret key token
- kaniko: Dockerfile at repo root, context git://github.com/REPO.git#refs/heads/BRANCH, destinations docker.io/ronaldraygun/gait-detection:VERSION + :latest, --cache=true --cache-repo=ronaldraygun/cache, mount docker-hub-registry secret as /kaniko/.docker exactly like palm-reading. Pin kaniko executor to a version tag (e.g. v1.23.2), not :latest
- update-declarative-config: sed image tag in k8s/apexalgo-iad/gait/gait-detection-deployment.yml (ronaldraygun/gait-detection:0.1.3 -> new semver), commit+push with same git identity

Acceptance criteria:
1. File committed+pushed to declarative-config main
2. kubectl --kubeconfig=/home/coding/.kube/iad-ci.kubeconfig get workflowtemplate pose-detection-build -n argo-workflows succeeds

title: Fix fake/hardcoded metrics and unsafe error handling in App.tsx
description: App.tsx is the actual live entry component (index.html -> src/main.tsx -> App.tsx) and contains several concrete, verifiable bugs: (1) Line 278: const movementIntensity = Math.random() * 0.5 + 0.2; // Mock movement detection -- the Movement Intensity metric shown live in the UI (pose-metrics grid) and included in exported JSON is pure random noise, not derived from actual pose motion, despite README advertising Motion Tracking with velocity/acceleration analysis. (2) Line 287: poseDuration: (timestamp - (timestamp - 1000)) / 1000, // Mock duration -- this expression is a compile-time constant: (timestamp - (timestamp - 1000)) always equals 1000, so poseDuration always equals exactly 1, never reflecting real elapsed pose time. (3) Line 503 inside handleExport: duration: Date.now() - (Date.now() - 60000) -- same pattern, always evaluates to exactly 60000ms; every exported session file reports a fixed 60-second session duration regardless of actual session length. (4) Line 408: catch (err) { ... setError() } accesses .message on an untyped/unknown catch variable with no instanceof Error guard, unlike the correct pattern already used two blocks earlier in the same file at line 185 (const errorMessage = err instanceof Error ? err.message : ...). Given tsconfig.json has strict: true (which enables useUnknownInCatchVariables), this is a real type-safety gap, not just style. Acceptance criteria: movementIntensity is computed from actual frame-to-frame keypoint position deltas (pose history is already available via poseMetrics/currentPose state each frame -- track previous keypoints in a ref and compute a real magnitude-of-change metric) rather than Math.random(). poseDuration and the export session duration are computed from a real tracked start timestamp (e.g. a ref set when tracking/session begins) rather than the constant-collapsing expressions. The catch block at line ~406-408 uses the same instanceof Error guard pattern as line 185. Existing tests still pass; if no test currently covers processFrame or handleExport, add a minimal vitest test asserting movementIntensity is not derived from Math.random and that duration reflects elapsed time, not a hardcoded constant.

comments.author: cli
comments.text: Precise text for item 4 (lost shell-quoting on original description): line 406-408 reads: catch (err) { console.error(FrameProcessingError, err); setError(TemplateLiteral with err.message here) } -- err.message is accessed on the unknown catch variable with no instanceof Error narrowing, unlike line 185 in the same file.

title: Hygiene sweep: purge tracked artifacts, dead CI workflows, doc drift
description:
Automated hygiene sweep (2026-07-11 corpus-audit follow-up). Findings: run the script for details.

Steps:
1. git pull origin (merge only; NEVER force-push).
2. Run: bash ~/jeds-curated-skills/repo-hygiene/scripts/repo_hygiene.sh --json .
3. Apply ONLY these fixes, ONE COMMIT PER CATEGORY:
   a) add missing .gitignore entries (target/, node_modules/, __pycache__/, dist/, etc.)
   b) git rm --cached all tracked build artifacts and binaries (keep files on disk)
   c) delete tracked .github/workflows files (GitHub Actions are disabled estate-wide; CI is Argo Workflows)
   d) fix README version-badge / GitHub-Actions-badge drift
4. FORBIDDEN: touching source code, git stash (or stash drop), git clean, git reset, --no-verify, force-push. The dirty-working-tree and stash-pileup findings are REPORT-ONLY context - do not act on them.
5. If a pre-commit hook rejects a commit (e.g. a provenance/fixture hook), stop that category, leave it unfixed, and record the hook output in a comment.
6. Re-run the script. Acceptance: tracked build artifacts = 0, dead CI workflow files = 0, gitignore gaps = 0 (or explicitly noted as hook-blocked). Push to origin and put the final script summary in the close comment.

title: Remove dead/orphaned code: stale .backup files, broken src/index.tsx, duplicate SettingsPanel, unconditional debug components
description:
Concrete dead/orphaned code found via grep + diff audit (none of it is reachable from the real app entry index.html -> src/main.tsx -> App.tsx):

(1) src/services/PoseDetectionService.ts.backup (103 lines) is a stale, much older version of the current src/services/PoseDetectionService.ts (632 lines) -- diff shows substantially different content (missing motion tracking fields, different constructor). No .ts.backup extension is ever imported by TypeScript/Vite, so this is inert clutter.

(2) src/services/PoseSmoothingService.ts.backup is a byte-for-byte identical duplicate of src/services/PoseSmoothingService.ts (diff produces zero output) -- pure redundant file.

(3) src/index.tsx imports MainApplication from './components/MainApplication', but no such file exists anywhere in the repo (find src -iname 'MainApplication*' returns nothing). This file is not referenced by index.html (which loads src/main.tsx, not src/index.tsx), not in vite.config.ts, and not in package.json. It is a broken, unreachable entry point left over from an earlier/parallel build attempt.

(4) Two duplicate, unused SettingsPanel components exist: src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx and src/components/Settings/SettingsPanel.tsx. Neither is imported by App.tsx or any other file (grep -rn "SettingsPanel" src/ --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts across the whole tree only matches each file's own definition).

(5) App.tsx unconditionally renders two components explicitly commented as temporary: '{/* Diagnostic Component - Temporary for debugging */} <PoseDetectionDiagnostic />' and '{/* Simple Pose Test - Temporary for debugging */} <SimplePoseTest />'. There is zero import.meta.env.DEV or similar dev-only gating anywhere in src/ (grep -rn "import.meta.env" src/ returns nothing), so these debug-only components ship unconditionally to production users at gait.jedarden.com.

Acceptance criteria:
- Delete both .ts.backup files (confirm via grep that nothing imports the .backup path first).
- Either restore/wire up a real MainApplication component or delete the orphaned src/index.tsx; if src/index.ts (no 'x', the barrel-export file) is confirmed genuinely unused too (not referenced by package.json main/module/exports and not imported by tests), remove it as well, otherwise leave it and note why it's kept.
- Remove both unused SettingsPanel.tsx files, or wire exactly one of them into the app if settings functionality is desired (do not keep two dead duplicates either way).
- Gate PoseDetectionDiagnostic and SimplePoseTest behind an import.meta.env.DEV check (or remove them from App.tsx entirely) so they no longer render in production builds.
- npm run build and existing test suite still pass after cleanup.

title: Cypress E2E suite tests a UI that does not exist in App.tsx
description: Evidence: cypress/e2e/gait-detection-app.cy.ts references 55 distinct data-testid selectors (gait-detection-app, app-title, camera-selector, start-camera-button, stop-camera-button, gait-confidence, stride-length-value, cadence-value, calibration-dialog, export-dialog, person-1-gait-params, mobile-layout, sr-announcements, etc — grep -oh "data-testid=\"[^\"]*\"" cypress/e2e/gait-detection-app.cy.ts | sort -u). Only 6 data-testid attributes exist anywhere in src/ (start-button, stop-button, reset-button, export-button, confirm-export, error-message — in ControlPanel.tsx and ExportDialog.tsx), and even the overlapping ones use different id strings than cypress expects (cypress wants start-camera-button/stop-camera-button, src has start-button/stop-button; cypress wants confirm-export-button, src has confirm-export). App.tsx itself (the actual entry rendered via index.html -> src/main.tsx -> App.tsx) has zero data-testid attributes. The cypress spec appears written against an aspirational multi-person gait-analysis UI (calibration dialog, per-person gait parameters, responsive breakpoints, accessibility announcements) that was never wired into the shipped App.tsx — none of GaitAnalysisPanel.tsx, GaitDetectionSystem.ts, or the Settings/Calibration UI are imported by App.tsx or main.tsx. Net effect: npm run test:e2e currently cannot pass a meaningful fraction of its assertions against the real app. Acceptance criteria: (1) Run npm run test:e2e (or npx cypress run) against the actual dev server and record which specs/assertions fail due to missing selectors. (2) Add data-testid attributes to App.tsx and/or its rendered children (CameraSelector, ControlPanel, error banner, video/canvas container) for every UI element that IS actually implemented today, matching the naming cypress already expects where reasonable (e.g. start-camera-button, camera-status, video-container, error-message, pose-confidence) rather than renaming cypress ids arbitrarily. (3) For assertions/describe blocks that reference features not implemented in the current App (multi-person tracking, gait calibration dialog, stride/cadence/symmetry gait parameters, mobile/tablet/desktop responsive layout testids, sr-announcements) either remove them or mark them .skip with a comment pointing at the missing feature — do not fabricate fake DOM just to satisfy the assertion. (4) npm run test:e2e passes cleanly (no failures) after the change, and any skipped specs are clearly annotated with why. Keep scope to test-id reconciliation + removing/skipping dead assertions; do NOT attempt to build the full aspirational multi-person/calibration UI in this bead.
